Primary Question: Is this extracted article technically usable and trustworthy enough to enter the annotation pipeline?
What Must Be Built: Automated rule engine for title/body/date/canonical/source/provenance/GCS checks; extraction-quality scoring; exception queue; parser-version linkage
Automation / Pre-Annotation: Fully automated first pass using deterministic validation and anomaly rules across 100% of records
Human Review: Small human audit sample plus review of flagged anomalies/failures; humans validate the automation, not label every record
Suggested Database Objects: automated_annotations or extraction_quality_reviews linked to article_versions; auto_status, auto_reasons, rule_version, confidence, validation_status
Reviewer UI: /review/l0 focused on sampled audit and exceptions rather than routine manual labeling
Quality / Evaluation: Automated pass/review/fail rates by source; sampled human validation accuracy; parser-defect rate; false-pass/false-fail rate
Entry Criterion: Collected article version exists with provenance
Exit Criterion: Automated L0 decision stored for 100% of records; validation sample shows acceptable performance; unresolved hard failures excluded
Downstream Use: Automated corpus-quality gate before all semantic layers
Proposal / Research Link: Preprocessing, provenance verification and data-quality control

Primary Question: Is the article substantively about a Kenyan event or issue within the study population?
What Must Be Built: Gazetteer/NER evidence engine plus geographic relevance classifier; confidence thresholds; uncertainty queue
Automation / Pre-Annotation: Automated across 100% using Kenyan place/institution/demonym evidence, foreign-location evidence, NER and a classifier/score; publisher identity alone must not decide
Human Review: Small stratified validation sample across sources/languages/confidence bands; ambiguous/low-confidence cases prioritized for human review
Suggested Database Objects: automated_annotations (task_type=kenya_relevance) + human_validation; preserve suggested_label, confidence, evidence, model/rule version
Reviewer UI: /review/l1 for sample validation and uncertainty review, showing article, detected evidence and automated label
Quality / Evaluation: Accuracy/F1 against human validation sample; ambiguity rate; confidence calibration; subgroup error rate by source/language
Exit Criterion: Automated Kenya-relevance label exists for all eligible records and validation performance is acceptable
Proposal / Research Link: Target population = eligible articles reporting/discussing Kenyan events/issues

Primary Question: Does the eligible Kenyan article report or substantively discuss GBV under the approved study definition?
Label Structure: Binary model (`not_gbv=0`, `gbv=1`) + application uncertainty label `borderline`; raw confidence is p(GBV)
What Must Be Built: Weak supervision, protected human review, reviewed-only/mixed-effective dataset export, class-weighted AfroXLMR training, checksummed offline model loading and persisted inference are implemented. Immediate remaining engineering work: install/verify L2 schema objects, recover the interrupted run and finish 24 pending predictions. Research work: expand independently reviewed positives, freeze reference membership, validate/calibrate thresholds.
Automation / Pre-Annotation: Weak machine coverage is 324/324 = 7/15/302. Human review of all 302 original borderline rows gives effective weak view 10/312/2. Reviewed export is 300 = 3/297; mixed-effective is 322 = 10/312. Trained `l2-afroxlmr-dev-v1` produced 300/324 persisted compatible model outputs = 10 gbv / 284 not_gbv / 6 borderline, leaving 24 pending.
Human Review: Weak-label review is recorded for the 302 originally borderline records; all 300 persisted transformer results are currently unreviewed. Future review should prioritize predicted positives, uncertainty/disagreement and underrepresented source/language groups while preserving a separate independent held-out reference set.
Suggested Database Objects: automated_annotations + human_validations + immutable reviewed/mixed development manifests now; future validation_samples/adjudications/frozen reference membership; preserve exact model, annotation, prerequisite, guideline and content-hash lineage
Reviewer UI: /annotations/l2 and /annotations/review/<annotation_id> support weak/model views, effective-vs-machine labels and protected review. Private readiness/priority tooling supports bounded inference and review prioritization; dedicated reference-freeze/adjudication workflow remains future work.
Quality / Evaluation: Current training loss/inference counts are engineering diagnostics, not accuracy. Final evaluation requires independent human-reference precision/recall/F1, macro-F1/AUC where supported, calibration/threshold analysis, false-positive/negative review and source/language subgroup metrics.
Exit Criterion: 324/324 current compatible model coverage plus protected independent human-reference evaluation demonstrating acceptable performance/calibration and documented error boundaries
When to Build: Initial model/export complete; resolve schema and 24 pending now; active learning/retraining and independent validation next while scaling toward ≥5,000
Downstream Use: GBV candidate selection for L3/L4, active learning and later analytics
Proposal / Research Link: Objective 1; development model implemented, research validation gate still open

Human Review: Small stratified validation sample including rare classes, multi-label cases and low-confidence predictions; humans correct sampled outputs
Suggested Database Objects: model_predictions/automated_annotations with per-label probabilities, threshold version, model_version; human_validation and final_reference_labels separate
Reviewer UI: /review/l3 for validating sampled multi-label outputs, low-confidence cases and rare categories
Quality / Evaluation: Per-label precision/recall/F1, macro/micro-F1, label-support/imbalance analysis, calibration and human override rate
Entry Criterion: L2 automated GBV-positive or borderline record
Exit Criterion: Multi-label predictions stored for all included records with acceptable validation metrics and documented thresholds
When to Build: After L2 classifier baseline is available
Downstream Use: Automated GBV-type analytics and training/evaluation target
Proposal / Research Link: Proposal requires one or more applicable GBV-type categories

What Must Be Built: Gazetteer/rule place-extraction baseline, contextual NER, event-location role classifier, Kenyan gazetteer/disambiguation and geocoding

Human Review: Design a human span/event-role/geocode annotation protocol; sample multi-location, ambiguous, low-confidence and source/language-diverse positives. Separate NER span correctness, event-vs-context role correctness and geocoding correctness.
Suggested Database Objects: future location_predictions / extracted_locations / geocoded_locations + human_validation; preserve span offsets, event role, normalized name/admin unit, confidence and model/geocoder versions
Reviewer UI: /review/l4 planned; reuse current review security/lineage principles with highlighted spans and candidate admin units
Quality / Evaluation: Entity precision/recall/F1 and exact-span match; event-role accuracy/F1; administrative-unit geocoding accuracy against human reference annotations
Entry Criterion: Initial usable L2-positive candidate pool for baseline; validated L2-positive set for final evaluation
Exit Criterion: Automated location outputs produced with acceptable independent span/role/geocode validation and documented error boundaries
When to Build: Baseline design/build can start now in parallel with L2 validation, L3 and corpus growth
Downstream Use: Location model evaluation and privacy-safe map aggregation
Proposal / Research Link: Objective 2: place extraction → event-location interpretation → geocoding

Label Structure: Multi-label privacy-risk flags + automated action + confidence
What Must Be Built: Automated PII/risk detection using NER + regex/rules + location-precision checks; suppression/generalization policy
Automation / Pre-Annotation: Automated across 100% before downstream display/API. Use high-recall PII detection and rule-based output actions
Human Review: Small high-risk audit sample plus mandatory review of low-confidence/conflicting cases where policy requires it
Suggested Database Objects: privacy_risk_predictions / safety_flags + human_validation; action, reason, confidence, policy_version, model_version
Reviewer UI: /review/l5 for sampled high-risk validation and policy exceptions
Quality / Evaluation: Recall on known sensitive patterns, false-negative audit, override rate, audit completeness, zero unnecessary PII in public outputs
Exit Criterion: Automated safety decision attached to every displayable record; validation confirms acceptable protection
When to Build: Design alongside L2-L4; enforce before dashboard
Proposal / Research Link: Proposal requires data minimisation, privacy protection, aggregated geography and human oversight

Primary Question: How well do automated annotations match human judgement, and where does automation fail?
Label Structure: confirmed/corrected/unresolved decision + human label + error type + adjudicated/frozen reference label where available
What Must Be Built: Protected review workspace is implemented; reviewed/mixed L2 export is implemented. Future work: stratified/uncertainty/disagreement sampling, independent reference-set freeze, reviewer assignment/adjudication and calibration reports.
Automation / Pre-Annotation: Current L2 weak review covers every originally borderline weak record, but the 300 persisted transformer predictions are unreviewed. Automation should prioritize predicted positives, uncertainty/disagreement and underrepresented source/language groups while excluding frozen reference members from active learning.
Human Review: Weak L2: 302 reviews recorded (300 corrected, 2 confirmed borderline). Model L2: 0/300 reviewed. L0 has 0 reviews and L1 has 1 correction. Future human review must add representative confidently classified cases and an independent held-out reference subset; full-corpus manual correction is not required.
Suggested Database Objects: human_validations + reviewed/mixed manifests now; future validation_samples, annotation_adjudications, reviewer metadata and frozen reference membership
Reviewer UI: Current review UI supports L0/L1/L2 confirm/correct/history; future sampling/adjudication/reference-freeze workflow should reuse the same exact-lineage/security model
Quality / Evaluation: Human-human agreement on any double-coded subset; automated-vs-human accuracy/F1 on independent samples; override/correction rate; calibration; error taxonomy; source/language subgroup metrics
Exit Criterion: Independent validation statistics and known error boundaries documented; final held-out reference subset frozen and isolated before thesis evaluation
Downstream Use: Human-supervised development, active learning, calibration and independent evaluation without manually labelling the full corpus

Suggested Database Objects: private development manifests now; future dataset_versions, corpus_membership, split_assignment, duplicate_group_id, model_version, annotation_version and guideline_version
Reviewer UI: Future admin/report view should show corpus/model versions, counts, duplicate groups and reference/split status without exposing private article text
Quality / Evaluation: No train/reference leakage; complete lineage; exact/near-duplicate control; reproducible manifests/artifacts; isolated held-out human reference set
Exit Criterion: Immutable research development/reference memberships and duplicate-aware splits exist before final comparison/evaluation
